questions.explanation: Plants are stacked by SRMC; the market dispatches up the stack until demand is met.

questions.prompt: In a pay-as-clear market, the single clearing price is set by…
choices: The marginal (last, most expensive) unit dispatched
questions.explanation: The marginal unit's SRMC sets the price paid to *all* accepted sellers — the defining feature of marginal pricing.

questions.prompt: Electricity needs a *sequence* of markets (forward → day-ahead → intraday → balancing) chiefly because…
choices: It can barely be stored and supply must match demand every instant
Regulators require four separate auctions by law
Each fuel type trades in its own market
Prices are fixed a year in advance
questions.explanation: Non-storability plus instantaneous balancing means players must keep re-balancing as forecasts sharpen toward delivery.

questions.prompt: Negative wholesale prices typically occur when…
choices: Inflexible must-run and subsidised output exceeds demand
A large power plant trips offline
questions.explanation: When output that can't (or won't) switch off exceeds demand, generators pay to keep running rather than shut down and restart.

choices: Pay resources to be available at peak (resource adequacy)
Sell more energy at lower prices
questions.explanation: It rewards availability — the 'missing money' an energy-only market may not provide for rarely-used capacity.

questions.prompt: To explain why tomorrow's 18:00 price is €90/MWh, the most direct step is to…
choices: Identify the marginal unit and compute its SRMC
Look only at total installed wind
questions.explanation: The clearing price ≈ the SRMC of the price-setting (marginal) unit for that hour.

questions.prompt: Two coupled bidding zones suddenly show *different* day-ahead prices. The most likely cause is…
choices: The interconnector between them has congested
One zone switched off its market
Both zones burned the same fuel
questions.explanation: Market coupling equalises prices until the link hits its capacity limit; congestion then splits the prices.

questions.prompt: Adding lots of near-zero-cost solar and wind tends to…
choices: Lower average wholesale prices (the merit-order effect)
Raise the SRMC of every plant
Eliminate the need for a balancing market
Increase fuel costs for gas plants
questions.explanation: Cheap renewables displace expensive plants and shift the marginal unit leftward, pulling average prices down.

questions.prompt: A wind developer signs a 10-year fixed-price **PPA** mainly to…
choices: Hedge spot-price volatility and secure financing
questions.explanation: A PPA locks in revenue, de-risking the project so banks will finance it — sidestepping volatile spot prices.

questions.prompt: A rising CO₂ price that lifts the **clean spark spread above the clean dark spread** causes…
choices: Gas to undercut coal in the merit order (fuel switching)
Coal to become cheaper than gas
questions.explanation: When gas's carbon-adjusted margin beats coal's, gas runs ahead of coal — fuel switching that lowers emissions.

questions.prompt: The short-run marginal cost of a thermal plant is…
questions.explanation: Fuel and carbon costs are divided by efficiency to express them per MWh of electricity, plus variable O&M.

questions.prompt: The **spark spread** of a gas plant is…
questions.explanation: Power price minus the efficiency-adjusted gas cost — the gross margin per MWh before carbon.

questions.prompt: The **clean** spark spread differs from the plain spark spread by…
questions.explanation: The clean spark spread nets out the cost of emission allowances to give the true margin.
